title: Finance & Accounts Adventure 2: Ratio Analysis
welcome_lead: Today you'll compute the current ratio, ROCE and gearing — three lenses on a firm.
meta_desc: Business Management Finance: current ratio (liquidity), ROCE (profitability), gearing (leverage).
final_note: You calculated three financial ratios and interpreted each for liquidity, profitability and leverage.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Can the firm pay its bills?

Current ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities. Healthy = 1.5–2.0.

Acid test = (Current Assets − Stock) / Current Liabilities. Strips out slow-moving stock; healthy ≥ 1.

A ratio under 1 risks insolvency; over 3 suggests idle cash.

ROCE = Operating Profit / Capital Employed × 100.

Capital employed = total equity + long-term liabilities.

ROCE tells investors how efficiently capital is converted into profit. Compare to the cost of capital and to industry peers.

Gearing = Long-term Debt / Capital Employed × 100.

Under 25% — low gearing, safe but missing leverage. Over 50% — high gearing, vulnerable to interest rate rises.

High gearing magnifies returns when profits grow and losses when they shrink — financial leverage.

Hygiene factors and motivators are just two types of motivation that combine.

Hygiene factors only prevent dissatisfaction (their absence demotivates, presence is neutral); motivators create satisfaction (their presence motivates, absence is neutral). They affect different outcomes, not different points on one scale.
